claim_text: EasyEquities says a security incident affected some of its systems
summary: EasyEquities says it became aware of a security incident affecting some of its systems and is investigating it with independent specialists. It emailed every client about it on Nov 26.
detail: The company has not said when it found the incident, which systems were affected or how it happened.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "We've become aware of a security incident affecting some of our systems, and we're investigating it with independent specialists"; TechCentral quotes the same words from the client email.

claim_text: EasyEquities has restricted client logins and is keeping its platform offline
summary: As a precaution, EasyEquities restricted client login and some services on Nov 26 and is keeping the platform offline while it completes checks. Clients cannot log in or view their accounts, and it has given no date for access to return.
detail: The restriction applies to all client accounts, including child accounts managed by a guardian. EasyEquities says it is restoring systems step by step and some products may come back before others.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "we've restricted access to client login and some services, so you can't log in or view your account right now"; "We're keeping the platform offline"; "some products may come back before others".

claim_text: EasyEquities says client funds and assets are accounted for
summary: EasyEquities says that, based on its investigation so far, client funds and assets are accounted for and secure, and that it will tell clients if that changes.
detail: This is the company's own account; no regulator or outside party has said so. The help page adds that its chief executive has also told clients their assets are safe.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page (updated Nov 27): "Based on our investigation to date, client funds and assets are accounted for and secure. The investigation is ongoing, and we'll tell you if that changes."

claim_text: EasyEquities has not said whether personal information was taken
summary: EasyEquities says it is assessing whether any personal information may have been accessed and will contact clients directly if it may have been.
detail: Later on Nov 27 TechCentral reported that EasyEquities sent clients a formal data-protection notice saying a small number of accounts were specifically looked up or targeted (c017). It has still not said what information, if any, was taken.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "We're assessing whether any personal information may have been accessed. If it may have been, we'll contact you directly"; TechCentral: the email did not say "whether client information had been accessed".

claim_text: EasyEquities says the incident is not related to its recent brand refresh
summary: EasyEquities says the security incident is not related to its recent brand refresh.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "This incident is not related to our recent brand refresh"; TechCentral reports the same.

claim_text: EasyEquities says the incident is not related to the September breach at a provider
summary: EasyEquities says this incident is not related to the September 2026 incident at a third-party service provider.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral quotes the company's Nov 26 update: the incident is not related to the one "involving a third-party service provider experienced in September 2026".

claim_text: Clients can trade through the trading desk; withdrawals reopen only after payment checks
summary: While logins are restricted, EasyEquities says clients can place trades through its trading desk by phone or email, and that withdrawals will reopen only once each payment provider has passed a test transaction with it.
detail: The trading desk cannot place investments on EasyProperties or EasyCrypto. Until Nov 27 the page said only that some withdrawals may be delayed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "you can contact our trading desk directly for assistance with placing your trades" and "Withdrawals reopen only once each payment provider has passed a test transaction with us".

claim_text: EasyEquities warns clients to watch for scam messages that claim to come from it
summary: EasyEquities tells clients to treat any unexpected call, email, SMS or WhatsApp asking for personal or banking details with caution, even if it seems to come from the company, and says it will never ask for a password, PIN or one-time code.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "treat any unexpected call, email, SMS or WhatsApp that asks for personal or banking details with caution, even if it seems to come from us" and "EasyEquities will never ask for your password, PIN, OTP or any code".

claim_text: EasyEquities says it has reported the incident to the Information Regulator and the FSCA
summary: TechCentral reports that EasyEquities told clients on Nov 27 it had reported the incident to the Information Regulator and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority. Its help page says only that it is working through its obligations.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral: "The company said it had reported the incident to the Information Regulator and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA)"; help page: "We're working through our legal and regulatory obligations".
notes: Until Nov 27 this row read "EasyEquities has not said whether it has told regulators" (Confirmed on the help page). Relabelled Reported because the new fact comes from one outlet's account of the client notice.

claim_text: An identity-verification provider used by EasyEquities was breached in September 2026
summary: In September 2026 a provider EasyEquities used for identity verification, which TechCentral names as RelyComply, said an unauthorised party had got into its systems. EasyEquities said its own systems were not breached.
detail: TechCentral reports that a ransomware group calling itself Dire Wolf claimed the RelyComply breach, which affected several South African financial firms. That is the group's claim.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: September page: the provider confirmed "an unauthorised third party had gained access to its environment"; "no evidence that EasyEquities' or Purple Group's own systems were breached". TechCentral names RelyComply.

claim_text: SA Home Loans said this week that an unknown attacker got into some of its systems
summary: TechCentral reports that home-loan provider SA Home Loans told customers this week that an unknown attacker had accessed some of its systems, including one used for collections. No source links it to the EasyEquities incident.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral: "This week, home loan provider SA Home Loans told customers that an unknown attacker had accessed some of its systems, including one used for collections".

claim_text: EasyEquities is an online investment platform owned by JSE-listed Purple Group
summary: EasyEquities is a South African online investment platform for buying shares, ETFs and other investments with any amount. It is owned by JSE-listed Purple Group, which says its brands serve more than 1.3 million people.
detail: Purple Group's results to Aug 31, 2026 give 1.316 million active clients for its Easy group.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Purple Group: "Our brands give more than 1.3 million people access to investing" and "Active clients 1.316m"; EasyEquities: "a subsidiary of Purple Group Limited, a company listed on the JSE Limited".

claim_text: Some outlets describe it as an apparent cyberattack
summary: EWN calls it EasyEquities' "second apparent cyberattack" in three months, and TechCentral's summary calls it a cyberattack. The company's own words are "a security incident affecting some of our systems".
label: Reported
why_it_supports: EWN: "second apparent cyberattack in the space of three months"; TechCentral's summary: "EasyEquities says it's been the victim of a cyberattack", while its quotes from the company say only "security incident".

claim_text: EasyEquities has published its plan for bringing the platform back
summary: EasyEquities says it is securing forensic evidence, checking balances against its custodian's and banks' records, rebuilding its login system with new keys and giving every connection, including partner apps, new access keys.
detail: It says each step is signed off by its security team with oversight from independent forensic specialists, and that clients may need to reset their password when sign-in reopens. It calls the steps its current plan and gives no dates.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page: "Securing digital forensic evidence from our systems"; "Rebuilding our login system with new keys"; "Giving every connection to our platform new access keys, including partner apps"; "you may need to reset your password".

claim_text: Partner apps may ask clients to link their EasyEquities account again
summary: EasyEquities says every connection to its platform, including partner apps, is getting new access keys, so some partner apps may ask clients to link their account again: only inside the partner app, never via an email or SMS link.
detail: It also says that once login is back clients can add two-factor authentication with an authenticator app or a passkey.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page (14:05 Nov 27): "Some partner apps may ask you to link your EasyEquities account again. Only do this inside the partner app itself, never through a link in an email or SMS."

claim_text: EasyEquities says it cannot promise compensation to clients who lose out because they could not trade
summary: EasyEquities says clients who lose out because they cannot trade can lodge a complaint under its complaints process, but that while the investigation is under way it cannot say what the outcome would be and cannot promise compensation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Help page (14:05 Nov 27): "You can lodge a complaint with us ... While the investigation is under way we can't say what the outcome would be, and we can't promise compensation."

claim_text: EasyEquities told clients a small number of accounts were specifically looked up or targeted
summary: TechCentral reports that on Nov 27 EasyEquities sent clients a formal notice under South Africa's data-protection law saying a "small number" of accounts were specifically looked up or targeted.
detail: TechCentral says the notice is made under section 22 of the Protection of Personal Information Act, which requires a company to tell people when there are reasonable grounds to believe their personal information was accessed or acquired without authorisation. EasyEquities says clients it does not contact separately have "no indication" their accounts were individually targeted. It has not said how many clients, or what information was exposed. Its help page, at our check, still said only that it was assessing whether personal information may have been accessed.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral quotes the notice: "So far, we have identified a small number of clients whose individual accounts were specifically looked up or targeted, and we are contacting those clients directly."

claim_text: EasyEquities says the attacker's initial access route was closed on Nov 25
summary: TechCentral reports that EasyEquities' Nov 27 notice says the attacker's "initial access route" was closed, and internet access to the affected server blocked, on Nov 25. It has not said when the intrusion began or how the attacker got in.
detail: TechCentral says the company also told clients it does not yet know who is responsible, and has not said whether ransomware or an extortion demand was involved. The company's own help page calls it "a security incident affecting some of our systems".
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral: "The notice says the attacker's 'initial access route' was closed, and internet access to the affected server blocked, on 25 November"; the company "did not yet know who was responsible".

claim_text: Purple Group told shareholders it identified the incident on Nov 25
summary: TechCentral reports that Purple Group told shareholders in a JSE announcement on Nov 27 that it identified the incident on Nov 25 and is establishing whether personal information was accessed.
detail: We have not found the JSE announcement itself; this is as TechCentral reports it. Clients were first told of the incident by email on Nov 26.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral: Purple Group "told shareholders in a JSE Sens announcement that it had identified the incident on 25 November" and "is establishing whether any personal information has been accessed".

claim_text: EasyEquities says it replaced keys, passwords and partner credentials and paused automated withdrawals
summary: TechCentral reports that EasyEquities says it replaced security keys, passwords and partner credentials and access tokens that may have been exposed, took more systems off the internet and paused automated withdrawals until checks are done.
detail: It is reviewing account activity "for any signs of unauthorised access or transactions". Clients who need urgent access to their money can contact it through its support portal, and all clients will have to create new passwords when the platform returns. It repeats that client funds are accounted for (c003).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TechCentral: it "replaced security keys and passwords as well as 'partner integration credentials and access tokens that may have been exposed'"; "Automated withdrawals have been paused and will be processed once checks are complete."
